title: HelixForge onboarding sprint-zero staffing and runbook kickoff
summary: Introductory sprint-zero kickoff to align on staffing, staging, security handoffs and runbook ownership for HelixForge's pilot of Redwood Inference. Covered VPC networking, SSO/KMS questions, test plans and a proposed 6-week pilot cadence.

Priya Singh: Draft success criteria doc for pilot (latency targets, QPS, error budgets) - due 2026-09-21
Daniel Kwong: Confirm network egress rules and proxy details for VPC peering - due 2026-09-18
next_steps: Redwood to send sprint-zero runbook template and onboarding slide deck
Schedule 1-hour staging walkthrough next week (Liam + Daniel + Maya)
Agree finalize pilot start date once infra details arrive (target week of 2026-09-27)
Redwood to open shared benchmark spreadsheet and invite HelixForge team
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Time: 16:00 UTC (52 minutes)
Attendees: Sofia Park (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Head Eng, HelixForge), Daniel Kwong (DevOps), Priya Singh (PM), Evan Reed (CTO)

Summary: kickoff for sprint-zero onboarding. goals: staff assignment, runbook, staging scope, network and security handoffs, define pilot success metrics.

Topics (auto): staffing, VPC & networking, SSO/KMS, benchmarking, runbook, timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to run through sprint-zero so we can get HelixForge into staging as quickly as possible. I think we have about 50 minutes. quick intros?
[00:18] Maya Ortiz: Maya here, head of eng at HelixForge. we'll be leading the pilot, working with our devops to get infra ready.
[00:27] Daniel Kwong: Daniel, devops. i'll be the point for VPC and networking.
[00:33] Priya Singh: Priya, product, i'll own success criteria and reporting.
[00:38] Evan Reed: Evan, CTO. i'm mostly here for alignment and risk questions.
[00:43] Liam Chen: Liam from Redwood, solutions engineering. i'll own the staging walkthrough and benchmark checklist.
[00:48] Sofia Park: cool, thanks. quick agenda: staffing & roles, infra checklist (VPC, peering, egress), auth (SSO/SAML, RBAC), runbook/rollback, perf baselines, timeline.

[02:15] Maya Ortiz: starting with staffing, we have a small infra team, two SREs, plus one backend lead. we need to confirm how much handholding for the first week.
[02:28] Liam Chen: for sprint-zero we usually advise one SE from us paired with your devops for the first 3 days to do the VPC peering and certs. after that handoff to your SREs.
[02:42] Daniel Kwong: fine, that's doable. question: do you need a dedicated account or can we use a sandbox under our existing org?
[02:50] Liam Chen: either works. sandbox is fine for initial tests, but for more realistic perf we recommend dedicated staging with the same network egress rules. also if you want private deployment later, the VPC setup matters.

[05:05] Priya Singh: on success criteria, we want 95th percentile latency under 300ms for small prompts and cost per 1k tokens under $0.60 — can you provide historical baselines?
[05:20] Liam Chen: we can share model-specific profiles. note some of the numbers depend on batching and KV cache usage. we can propose a config that meets your latency target for the pilot.
[05:35] Evan Reed: on security: SOC 2 is a baseline for us. we also need audit logs for requests and key rotation via KMS. how do you handle customer key material?
[05:48] Sofia Park: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs, and Dedicated has isolation guarantees. we'll follow up with our security pack but high level: you can bring your own KMS for private deployments.

[08:10] Maya Ortiz: does Redwood do SAML mapping for groups so we can map to RBAC in console?
[08:18] Liam Chen: yes, we support SAML and SCIM for provisioning. mapping groups to roles is supported, sometimes the attribute names come through differently so we validate in the staging handshake.

[11:05] Daniel Kwong: networking specifics: we use NAT gateways and a forward proxy. will that break anything with peering?
[11:14] Liam Chen: forward proxies are common; we'll need IP ranges and egress rules for the inference nodes. also if you're restricting egress to specific endpoints we need to allow Redwood control plane endpoints for management and metrics.
[11:30] Daniel Kwong: ok i'll pull the list of endpoints.

[14:40] Priya Singh: runbook question — what's the rollback strategy if a model variant causes bad outputs in prod?
[14:50] Liam Chen: canary deploys and automatic fallback to a previous pinned model variant are standard. runbook includes steps to pin versions, circuit-breaker thresholds and how to roll back traffic. we'll share a template.
[15:05] Evan Reed: curious about telemetry retention — we need logs for 12 months for audits, is that doable?
[15:12] Sofia Park: retention tiers are configurable; for Private deployments you can store logs in your S3 and retain as needed. for Hosted we have add-on retention packages. we'll include options in the security doc.

[18:00] Maya Ortiz: performance testing — we want a stress test that simulates peak QPS and typical burst patterns. how do we coordinate the load generation?
[18:12] Liam Chen: we can share a load test harness and a spreadsheet with scenario configs. SE will run the first pass with you and then hand over the scripts. we usually test at several sequence lengths to map cost/latency curves.

[22:45] Priya Singh: timeline — we're aiming for a 6-week pilot: week 0 (this onboarding), week 1 staging + benchmarks, week 2-4 pilot tweaks, week 5 evaluation, week 6 decision to expand. does that align with your expectations?
[22:58] Sofia Park: yes that looks good; we'll plan checkpoints at week 1, week 3 and pre-eval at week 5.

[26:10] Daniel Kwong: what's the expected SE time commitment during week 1? a full-day pairing or just a couple hours?
[26:20] Liam Chen: typically two half-day sessions or one full day to get peering and certs completed, then daily 30-minute syncs for the first week.

[30:00] Maya Ortiz: any blockers we should know about? we have a compliance review on the 24th of September that could affect timing if they need extra docs.
[30:12] Evan Reed: we'll surface any compliance asks quickly, but ideally we don't want to slip the pilot start past the week of 9/27.

[33:50] Liam Chen: quick note on model selection: for your use case (short response generation + reranking), we recommend a mid-sized quantized model to balance latency/cost. Redwood Optimize can give automatic quantization suggestions.
[34:05] Priya Singh: will Redwood run any evals against our prompt sets?
[34:13] Liam Chen: yes, we can run initial evals in staging — we'll need your prompt set and expected outputs, and we can run automated regression checks.

[38:40] Sofia Park: recap of immediate items: Maya to send infra diagram and AWS IDs; Daniel to provide proxy and egress rules; Liam to send staging checklist, benchmark harness and runbook template; Priya to draft success criteria doc.
[38:58] Maya Ortiz: i'll get those by end of week.

[41:00] Priya Singh: action on orgs/roles — i'll map our SSO groups to the desired RBAC and share with you for validation.
[41:10] Liam Chen: great, please include sample assertions from your identity provider.

[45:25] Evan Reed: question about data retention of request/response pairs for evals, can we opt out for any PII?
[45:36] Sofia Park: yes you can opt out and choose not to log request bodies. for evals we can use redacted prompt sets or run evals in your VPC/private deployment to keep data in-house.

[48:00] Daniel Kwong: final logistics: who will open the shared spreadsheet?
[48:06] Sofia Park: i'll create the benchmark spreadsheet and invite everyone after the call.

[50:10] Liam Chen: next sync — propose Tuesday 2026-09-22 16:00 UTC for staging walkthrough, i'll block 60 minutes.
[50:22] Maya Ortiz: works for us.

[51:00] Sofia Park: thanks all, we'll follow up with the runbook and security pack. action items in the notes. end call.

Action items (auto): see action_items above.

Links shared: onboarding-runbook-template.pdf (via email), benchmark-harness.zip (Redwood drive), security-pack-link (Redwood secure portal)

End of transcript.
